column1: # The English an affix gets in a word glossed by its parts (tunatale-h0q3.26). Hand-written.
# The owner approved this wording on 2026-10-28 (https://claude.ai/artifact/WNCxM9XxVTpje6ANtoyiRm,
# version 2): one short label per form, chosen by the kind of root it is on. A piece is spelled as
# the affix decoder spells it (mu-, -un, gi-an). The root kind is a subject from
# wolff_dictionary.decode_classes (what Wolff's class code makes the subject), or noun / adjective
# for a root with no verb senses, or verb / adjective for pa-. A piece with no row here is silent.
# The Wolff column cites his numbered sense, for the card's Details.
# Wolff's general i- ('what is used or moved', which an a or b code adds to nearly every verb
# and the Verb field shows dimmed) labels nothing: it would make every gi- ambiguous.
# A noun with no verb sense labels nothing either (Wolff's mu- 2a, 'added to nouns'): the decoder
# also 'finds' mi- + sor in misor, a form of address, and 'did + the south wind' is a confident
# wrong line. An adjective stands in (mu- 3a, 'become [adj.]').
